results.title: Automorphism of the regular rooted tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the vertices of the $d$-regular rooted tree are the finite words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$. A permutation $f$ of this set of words is a tree automorphism when, for all words $u$ and $v$, writing $|u|$ for the length of $u$ and $uv$ for the concatenation of $u$ and $v$, the word $f(u)$ has length $|u|$ and the first $|u|$ letters of $f(uv)$ form $f(u)$.

results.title: Section of a map of the regular rooted tree at a vertex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $f$ be a permutation of the finite words over $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$ (the vertices of the $d$-regular rooted tree) and let $u$ be a word, of length $|u|$. The section (state) of $f$ at $u$ is the map sending each word $w$ to the word obtained from $f(uw)$ by deleting its first $|u|$ letters, where $uw$ is the concatenation of $u$ and $w$.

results.title: Finite-state automorphism of the regular rooted tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a permutation $f$ of the finite words over $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$ is a finite-state automorphism of the $d$-regular rooted tree when it is an automorphism of the tree and the sections of $f$ at all vertices $u$ form a finite set of maps.

results.title: Automorphisms of the regular rooted tree (Kourovka 16.85)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number and let $X^*$ be the set of finite words over the alphabet $X = \{0, \dots, d-1\}$, the vertices of the $d$-regular rooted tree. A permutation $f$ of $X^*$ is a tree automorphism when, for all words $u$ and $v$, the word $f(u)$ has the same length $|u|$ as $u$ and the first $|u|$ letters of $f(uv)$ form the word $f(u)$, where $uv$ denotes concatenation.

results.title: Section of a permutation of the tree at a vertex (Kourovka 16.85)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $d$, let $X^*$ be the set of finite words over $X = \{0, \dots, d-1\}$, let $f$ be a permutation of $X^*$ and let $u \in X^*$, of length $|u|$. The section (state) of $f$ at $u$ is the map $X^* \to X^*$ sending a word $w$ to the word obtained from $f(uw)$ by deleting its first $|u|$ letters (all of them if it has fewer), where $uw$ denotes concatenation.

results.title: Finite-state automorphisms of the regular rooted tree (Kourovka 16.85)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $d$, let $X^*$ be the set of finite words over $X = \{0, \dots, d-1\}$. A permutation $f$ of $X^*$ is a finite-state automorphism when it is an automorphism of the $d$-regular rooted tree and its sections at the vertices $u \in X^*$ form a finite set of maps $X^* \to X^*$.

results.title: Faithful actions by finite-state tree automorphisms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ acts faithfully on a regular rooted tree by finite-state automorphisms when there are a natural number $d \ge 2$ and an injective group homomorphism $\varphi$ from $G$ to the group of permutations of the set of finite words over $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$ such that $\varphi(g)$ is a finite-state automorphism of the $d$-regular rooted tree for every $g \in G$.

results.title: Finite-state actions of free products (Kourovka Problem 16.85)

results.summary: The statement that for all groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ and $H$ each act faithfully on a regular rooted tree by finite-state automorphisms (the two trees may have different degrees), then so does their free product $G \ast H$.

results.title: Fedorova–Oliynyk theorem (Kourovka Problem 16.85)

results.summary: For all groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ and $H$ each act faithfully on a regular rooted tree by finite-state automorphisms, then their free product $G \ast H$ acts faithfully on some regular rooted tree by finite-state automorphisms.

results.title: Locally finite group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is locally finite when for every finite subset $S$ of $G$ the subgroup generated by $S$ is finite, that is, every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is finite.

results.title: Minimal condition on centralizers

results.title: The Zeckendorf-adic integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Zeckendorf-adic integers $\mathbb{X}$ are the digit sequences $x = (x_k)_{k \ge 0}$ with $x_k \in \{0, 1\}$ such that $x_0 = x_1 = 0$ and no two consecutive digits are both $1$, that is, $x_k x_{k+1} = 0$ for every $k$.

results.title: Zeckendorf digit sequence of a natural number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F_k$ be the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = F_2 = 1$). Every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ has a unique Zeckendorf representation $n = F_{k_1} + \dots + F_{k_m}$ with $k_1 > \dots > k_m \ge 2$ and no two consecutive indices. The Zeckendorf digit sequence of $n$ is the binary sequence $(x_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $x_k = 1$ if $k$ is one of the indices $k_1, \dots, k_m$ and $x_k = 0$ otherwise.

results.title: The Zeckendorf odometer
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The odometer is the map $T$ on digit sequences $x = (x_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $x_k \in \{0, 1\}$ defined as follows. If $x_k = x_{k+1} = 0$ for some $k \ge 2$, let $k$ be the least such index; then $T(x)_j = 0$ for $j < k$, $T(x)_k = 1$ and $T(x)_j = x_j$ for $j > k$. If there is no such $k$, then $T(x)$ is the zero sequence.

results.title: Zeckendorf digit sequence of zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Zeckendorf digit sequence of $0$ is the zero sequence: all of its digits are $0$, because the Zeckendorf representation of $0$ is empty.

results.title: The odometer on a point ending in $00$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a Zeckendorf-adic integer $x = (x_k)_{k \ge 2}$ has $x_2 = x_3 = 0$, then the odometer $T(x) = x + 1$ sets the unit digit $x_2$ to $1$ and leaves every other digit of $x$ unchanged.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be the Zeckendorf odometer and let $x = (x_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a digit sequence with $x_k \in \{0, 1\}$ such that for every $k \ge 2$ we have $x_k = 1$ or $x_{k+1} = 1$. Then $T(x)$ is the zero sequence.

results.title: Truncated variation of the Zeckendorf digit sum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $T$ be the Zeckendorf odometer $x \mapsto x + 1$ on binary sequences, and write $x + r = T^r(x)$ for its $r$-th iterate. For $r, k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a binary sequence $x = (x_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$, let $s_k(x) = x_2 + \dots + x_k$. The truncated variation is the integer $\Delta_k^{(r)}(x) = s_k(x + r) - s_k(x)$.

results.title: The truncated variation vanishes for zero steps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be the Zeckendorf odometer and, for a binary sequence $x$, let $s_k(x) = x_2 + \dots + x_k$ and $\Delta_k^{(r)}(x) = s_k(T^r(x)) - s_k(x)$. Then $\Delta_k^{(0)}(x) = 0$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every binary sequence $x$.

results.title: The variation of the Zeckendorf digit sum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and a digit sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1\}$, let $\Delta_k^{(r)}(x)$ be the truncated variation of order $k$. If the integer sequence $(\Delta_k^{(r)}(x))_k$ is eventually constant, the variation $\Delta^{(r)}(x) = \lim_{k \to \infty} \Delta_k^{(r)}(x)$ is its eventual value; otherwise $\Delta^{(r)}(x) = 0$.

results.title: The variation is the eventual value of the truncated variations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a binary sequence and let $d \in \mathbb{Z}$. If the truncated variation $\Delta_k^{(r)}(x)$ equals $d$ for all sufficiently large $k$, then the variation $\Delta^{(r)}(x)$ equals $d$.

results.title: The variation for $r = 0$ vanishes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every digit sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1\}$, not only for Zeckendorf-adic integers, the variation satisfies $\Delta^{(0)}(x) = 0$.

results.title: The Zeckendorf Markov chain
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio, and let $\psi(0, t) = 1$ if $t < 1/\varphi^2$, $\psi(0, t) = 0$ otherwise, and $\psi(1, t) = 0$. For a real sequence $(u_n)_{n \ge 0}$, written $u_n = U_{n+2}$, the chain $(y_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ is the sequence in $\{0, 1\}$ with $y_0 = y_1 = 0$ and $y_j = \psi(y_{j-1}, U_j)$ for $j \ge 2$; that is, $y_{n+2} = 1$ exactly when $y_{n+1} = 0$ and $u_n < 1/\varphi^2$.

results.title: Normalized cross product of genotype markers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The normalized cross product `r j k = X_jᵀ X_k / N` of markers `j` and `k`. For a standardized genotype matrix (`IsStandardized`) it is the sample correlation of the two markers; for other matrices it is only a scale-dependent dot product.

results.title: LD score of a marker
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The LD score `ℓ j = ∑ k, r j k ^ 2` of marker `j` (an LD score in the sense of the cited paper for a standardized genotype matrix).

results.title: Standardized genotype matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The genotype matrix is standardized: every marker column has mean `0` and sum of squares `N` (unit sample variance).

results.title: A standardized marker has correlation one with itself
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a standardized matrix each marker has correlation `1` with itself.

results.title: Correlations of standardized markers lie in (-1, 1)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a standardized matrix the correlations lie in `[-1, 1]` (Cauchy–Schwarz).

results.title: Random-effects model of LD-score regression
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: The random-effects model of LD-score regression (Bulik-Sullivan et al. 2015), stated at the level of raw second moments, for `N` individuals and `M` markers with heritability `h2`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of heritability in the LD-score model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The heritability is nonnegative when there is at least one marker.

results.title: Heritability is at most one in the LD-score model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The heritability is at most `1` when there is at least one individual.

results.title: Phenotype in the LD-score model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The phenotype `y = X β + ε`.

results.title: Normalized marginal score in the LD-score model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `N`-normalized score `β̂ j = X_jᵀ y / N` of marker `j`. For a standardized column (`∑ i, X i j ^ 2 = N`) it is the marginal least-squares estimate of the effect of marker `j`; in general that estimate has denominator `∑ i, X i j ^ 2` instead of `N`.

results.title: Association statistic in the LD-score model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The association statistic `χ² j = N * β̂ j ^ 2` of marker `j`.

results.title: Expected association statistic for an arbitrary genotype matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The exact expectation of the association statistic built from the `N`-normalized score, for an arbitrary genotype matrix: `𝔼[χ² j] = N h² / M * ℓ j + (1 - h²) * (∑ i, X i j ^ 2) / N`. (For `N = 0` both sides are `0` by the convention `x / 0 = 0`.)

results.title: LD-score regression
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: LD-score regression (Bulik-Sullivan et al. 2015): for a standardized genotype matrix (`IsStandardized`, so that `ldCorr` is the sample correlation and `ldScore` the LD score) and `N ≠ 0`, `𝔼[χ² j] = N h² / M * ℓ j + (1 - h²)`. The expected association statistic is affine in the LD score, with slope `N h² / M` and intercept `1 - h²`. The proof uses only that column `j` has sum of squares `N`; the rest of the…

results.title: Mean LD score
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mean LD score `ℓ̄ = (1 / M) ∑ j, ℓ j`.

results.title: Polygenic inflation of the mean association statistic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Polygenic inflation: for a standardized genotype matrix with `N, M ≠ 0`, the mean expected association statistic is `1 - h² + N h² ℓ̄ / M`.

results.title: Phenotype with population stratification
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The phenotype with a stratification shift: `y i = (X β) i + ε i + s * c i`.

results.title: Normalized score under stratification
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `N`-normalized score of marker `j` under stratification, `X_jᵀ y / N`.

results.title: Association statistic under stratification
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The association statistic `N * β̂ j ^ 2` under stratification.

results.title: Expected association statistic under stratification
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Stratification inflation: for a probability measure and mean-zero effects and noise, `𝔼[χ² j] = N h² / M * ℓ j + (1 - h²) (∑ i, X i j ^ 2) / N + N s² (X_jᵀ c / N)²`.

results.title: Expected statistic under stratification for standardized genotypes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Stratification inflation for a standardized genotype matrix and `N ≠ 0`: `𝔼[χ² j] = N h² / M * ℓ j + (1 - h²) + N s² (X_jᵀ c / N)²`.

results.title: LD-score regression with constant stratification
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With a constant stratification term (`s² (X_jᵀ c / N)² = a` for every marker), the expected statistic is exactly affine in the LD score, with slope `N h² / M` and intercept `1 - h² + N a`.

results.title: Mean association statistic with constant stratification
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With a constant stratification term `N a`, the mean expected statistic is `N h² ℓ̄ / M + (1 - h² + N a)`.

results.title: Attenuation ratio
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The attenuation ratio `(intercept - 1) / (mean χ² - 1)` of Loh et al. (2018).

results.title: Attenuation ratio under constant stratification
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With a constant stratification term `N a`, the attenuation ratio of the exact intercept `1 - h² + N a` and the mean expected statistic is `(N a - h²) / (N h² ℓ̄ / M + N a - h²)`.

results.title: Confounding share of inflation under constant stratification
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With a constant stratification term `N a`, the share of the mean inflation above the exact null level `1 - h²` that is due to stratification is `N a / (N a + N h² ℓ̄ / M)`.

results.title: Confounding share lies between 0 and 1
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The confounding share `N a / (N a + N h² ℓ̄ / M)` lies in `[0, 1]` when `a`, `h²` and `ℓ̄` are nonnegative (as they are in the model: `a` is a square, `h² ≥ 0` by `Model.h2_nonneg`, LD scores are sums of squares).
